Tagcast 0.75.0 brings public playlist import, more playlist controls, persistent lyrics and a clearer album editor to the desktop app and Python/browser version.

## Import and organise playlists

- **Playlist URL**, next to CSV import, reads public Deezer playlists and public ListenBrainz playlists as an experimental test source. Both use the existing local matching, manual choices and final private-playlist review. No source login or audio download is involved.
- **Pause import** saves up to 10 account-specific checkpoints / 64 MB, surviving restarts. Resume refreshes the library and rechecks matches while preserving unchanged manual choices. Closing an unfinished import asks before discarding it.
- CSV matching offers explicit copy preferences, including **FLAC first, then oldest year**. Album mapping explains when it restricts automatic matches to that album. Version differences still need review.
- Playlist cards/list rows and details show total duration. Browsing and searching reuse the loaded library. Name/description-only edits preserve every stored position and cover without replacing the track list.
- Search a playlist by title, artist or album across all pages, retaining original position numbers. A row's cross reviews removal of only that occurrence; the music library and current queue stay intact.
- **Reorder tracks** supports drag handles, keyboard arrows and **Move to position…**, with its own search. Moves remain local until **Save order**; **Cancel** discards them. Repeated and unavailable positions are preserved.

## Lyrics and editing

- The existing album editor now has **Edit album / Edit tracks** tabs. The track list scrolls independently beside the selected track's form; changing tabs preserves the draft and existing review.
- Native iBroadcast lyrics appear in Now playing. An explicit **Find lyrics on LRCLIB** offers a free fallback, with full-title/artist/duration matching and a separate public cache.
- **… → Check album lyrics** checks only the open album, one track at a time, up to 100 distinct tracks. Known nonempty text gets a subtle **Lyrics** button that opens a read-only viewer without playback or requests. Albums and playlists are never scanned automatically.
- Native lyrics and empty results persist locally across restarts, bound to the account and track identity, without timed expiry. Confirmed lyrics edits refresh the cache; uncertain saves invalidate it. Lyrics saving has a separate Premium review and preserves unrelated native userdata. Known free accounts retain reading and lookup while Premium-only controls stay hidden.
- Corrupt lyrics-cache initialization now closes the database connection on error, including on Windows.

## Playback, interface and community

- Remove individual play queue occurrences with a cross, including the last playing entry, while retaining access to the remaining queue.
- Playlist covers and larger artist photos provide image-editing overlays. Dialog controls and review spacing are more consistent, the sidebar uses an aligned separator, and library reloads cycle through eight playful messages beneath the clear loading heading.
- The README and **Settings → Community** link to **[r/Tagcast](https://www.reddit.com/r/Tagcast/)**. The Wiki is updated with the released workflows and 62 original screenshots from 22 October.
- The macOS desktop app retains the existing player and system audio output. For AirPlay, keep **System default** selected and choose the speaker through macOS Control Centre → Sound. Direct native AirPlay selection is not included; supported browsers retain their own native picker.

## Downloads and upgrading

- **macOS Apple Silicon:** `tagcast-0.75.0-macos-arm64.zip`.
- **macOS Intel:** `tagcast-0.75.0-macos-x64.zip`.
- **Windows x64:** `tagcast-0.75.0-windows-x64.zip`.
- **Linux x64:** `tagcast-0.75.0-linux-x64.tar.gz`.

Every archive has a SHA-256 companion. Keep the complete extracted package together.
**Quit the older Tagcast before starting 0.75.0.** Settings, sign-in and local account favourites remain in the existing Tagcast folder. Browser-local preferences and Change history remain separate from Electron's profile.

For Homebrew, quit Tagcast and run `brew update`, then `brew upgrade --cask cyberdeliaAI/apps/tagcast` after the cask has updated.

See the [installation guide](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/wiki/Getting-started) and [full user guide](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/wiki). Tagcast never changes local music files and does not install updates automatically.
